title: kv-cache: adaptive compaction + spillover-aware eviction to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Marco Rivera
description:
Context: We continue to see KV cache fragmentation and increased GPU paging under mixed-length workloads. This causes tail latency spikes and higher token cost due to frequent spillover and page faults when active sessions cause many small allocations. Goal: reduce fragmentation and paging, provide a spillover-aware eviction policy, and enable background compaction without impacting latency-critical paths.

What this PR does: Implements an adaptive compaction subsystem and a spillover-aware eviction policy in the serving runtime's KV cache. Key changes: 1) A lightweight background compactor that coalesces free segments when GPU utilization is low and memory pressure is high. It runs opportunistically and yields to inference threads. 2) Eviction policy augmentation: when spillover to host memory is triggered, evictions prefer cold fragments that will reduce fragmentation footprint and minimize future paging; hot prefixes are preserved via an age+weight heuristic. 3) Paging threshold tuning: dynamic thresholds for triggering spillover based on recent page-fault rates and tail-latency SLOs. 4) Metrics and tracing: new metrics (kv/compaction_cycles, kv/compacted_bytes, kv/eviction_spillover_count, kv/fragmentation_ratio) and tracing spans to correlate compaction runs with latency. 5) Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for compaction correctness, synthetic workloads for fragmentation, and canary bench harness results.

Design notes: The compactor operates on per-GPU arenas to avoid cross-device synchronization. We use an epoch-based allocator snapshot to avoid pausing inference; compaction moves cold entries to a new contiguous block and updates KV handles via CAS with a short retry window. Eviction scoring combines access recency (LRU-ish), prefix weight (sequence length estimate), and fragmentation impact score (estimated bytes reclaimed). The policy is pluggable and feature-gated.

Compatibility and migration: Default is disabled behind runtime flag kv.compaction.enabled=false. A staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) is recommended; migrations do not require on-disk format changes.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover compaction correctness and concurrent access; integration tests simulate mixed short/long sequence distributions and measure page-faults and tail-latency. Benchmarks show a 32% reduction in page faults and 12-18% improvement in p99 latency on a heavy mixed workload.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids synchronous compaction on hot paths; decisions were driven by observed production traces (SUP-4452). See linked linear tasks for follow-ups (shard-aware compaction, compaction throttling heuristics).

release_notes: Implements adaptive compaction and spillover-aware eviction to reduce KV cache fragmentation and GPU page faults. Adds metrics and tracing for compaction and eviction decisions. Feature-gated rollout. Impact: lower tail latency and reduced token cost under mixed-length workloads.
benchmarks_summary: Canary runs on 4x A100: page faults -32%, p99 latency -12% to -18% depending on workload mix. Small throughput overhead (<=1.5%) for compaction background cycles.
rollout_plan: Start canary in us-west-2 on 3 nodes with kv.compaction.enabled=true and observability flags. Monitor kv/compaction_cycles, kv/fragmentation_ratio, kv/eviction_spillover_count and tail-latency for 48h before increasing to 10%.
